clue.text: Fruit drinks to feed primate

indicators.note: the fruit drinks something in, so it takes the other piece inside itself

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to feed is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone offers fruit-flavoured drinks to nourish a monkey or ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks' looks like a noun after 'Fruit', but it is the verb of containment: the fruit takes in the feeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimps and orangutans are the large tailless primates grouped under this name.

clue.text: 2 used by secret agent in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution says the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters wanted are used by, so lie within, the words secret agent, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A spy turns an exit to his own ends during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'used' as the definition; the definition is '2', pointing at the answer to 2 down, and 'used by' is the hiding signal. Down clue: ETAG, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway or barrier opening that lets people leave is a way out, the meaning of clue 2.

clue.text: Leave cardinal in Rome, breaking heart of deity

indicators.note: the numeral breaks into the other letters, splitting them apart
the heart of a word is its central letters, here everything but the ends

parts.note: a cardinal number in Roman numerals: X is ten

explanation.surface: A cardinal departs Rome after shattering the core of a god's image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman in Rome, but it is a cardinal number written as a Roman numeral. 'heart of' gives EIT from deity, and 'breaking' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a place is to go out of it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bell rung by Jock's compatriot returning home

indicators.note: returning means the word for a fellow Scot is read backwards

parts.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, so his compatriot is a Scot
at home is in

explanation.surface: A Scotsman heading home sounds a bell for his fellow countryman.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is British slang for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or a signal rung on one to warn people.

clue.text: Royal places for wine to be produced

indicators.note: produced in the sense of made or brought out in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sites where wine will be made, as if describing vineyards.
explanation.walkthrough: The heir to the British throne traditionally holds this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title belongs to the eldest son of the British monarch, a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Who in Paris contributes to reduced service in underground?

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, contributing to it from inside
reduced means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a Mass is a church service
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's question about a cut-down service on the Paris Métro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground' suggests a railway; it is the resistance movement. MAS (Mass reduced) takes in QUI.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Resistance fighters of the Second World War were an underground movement known by this name.

clue.text: Upstanding girl admitted to stress creating hazard

indicators.note: the girl is admitted into the other word, going inside it

parts.note: accent means stress on a syllable

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Di is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An upright girl let into an emphasis causes danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' sounds like praise for the girl, but in a down clue it turns her name upside down before 'admitted to' puts her inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a chance mishap, and an accident is an unplanned harmful event.

clue.text: Wanton global alliance found to be internally sound

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a global alliance

indicators.note: internally means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: proved means found to be, as in proved true
sound means OK, all right

explanation.surface: A worldwide alliance turns out to be fine on the inside, yet reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanton attack is one made without provocation or cause, gratuitous and unjustified.

clue.text: Teams go off the way one may go up

definitions.text: the way one may go up

parts.note: sides are teams
addle means go bad, as an egg does

explanation.surface: Teams that go to pieces, and how someone climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up' suggests climbing; here it means mounting a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding with both legs on one side of the horse was the way women in skirts mounted and rode.

clue.text: Worst witch in Gryffindor keeps chasing the odd owl etc

indicators.note: the words keep the answer inside them, running across their gaps

explanation.surface: A Harry Potter-style tale: the worst witch in the house goes after owls.
explanation.walkthrough: The Worst Witch is a children's book series, and Gryffindor a house at Hogwarts. The answer runs from the end of 'worst' through 'witch in' to the start of 'Gryffindor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdwatching enthusiasts who rush to see rare birds are called twitchers, and their hobby is named this.

clue.text: Students here charm glamorous cooks, shedding uniform

indicators.note: cooks means messes about with, so these letters are rearranged
shedding means one letter is dropped from the mix

parts.note: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Students here sweet-talk stylish chefs, taking off their uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like school clothing; it is the letter U, struck from CHARMGLAMOROUS before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A selective state secondary school in Britain is where such pupils study.

clue.text: Bow merchant identified by three coppers, the last retired

indicators.note: the last of the coppers is retired, turned back, while the first two stay as they are

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper, P a penny (a copper coin), and DI a Detective Inspector, a police copper

explanation.surface: An archery dealer is recognised by three police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final copper, DI, turns round to ID; CU and P stay. 'Bow merchant' plays on a trader in bows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is pictured as an archer firing arrows from his bow.

clue.text: Pre-match requisites at Lord's — the game's a gamble

definitions.meaning: a cricket match needs a prepared strip and a coin flip before it starts
a gambling game where coins are thrown at a mark

explanation.surface: Before a cricket match at Lord's, a reminder that sport is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London home of cricket; before play the groundstaff prepare the pitch and the captains toss a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old gambling game in which players throw coins at a mark, the nearest winning.

clue.text: Dim criminal fell in and died

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim-witted crook fell in and perished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' looks like a description of the criminal, but it is the definition, meaning faint or blurred.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dim is faint and blurry, lacking clear outlines.

clue.text: Route travelled by boat, traditional follower of fish?

definitions.meaning: a ship's course on the open sea, the main
in a formal dinner the meat dish traditionally comes after the fish

explanation.surface: A boat's route, and the dish that usually comes after the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal dish of a meal follows the fish course; and a sea voyage path, with main meaning ocean.

clue.text: Six-footer heading to rear part of plane, perhaps

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, goes to the back of the word

parts.note: a flea is an insect, with six feet

explanation.surface: An insect heads for the tail end of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect; 'plane' suggests an aircraft but is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane tree has broad leaves, so one is a part of that tree.

clue.text: Usual commuter's first getting on — there's no cure for it!

parts.note: common means usual, ordinary

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: getting on means old, ageing

explanation.surface: An ordinary commuter boards the train, carrying an incurable bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' suggests boarding a train, but means growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday viral infection of nose and throat famously has no known remedy.

clue.text: Auntie studied what workers feed their youngsters

parts.note: Auntie and the Beeb are both nicknames for the BBC
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: An aunt researched what working parents give their children to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC, also called the Beeb. 'workers' are worker bees, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees feed larvae a mixture of pollen and honey stored in the hive.

clue.text: Academic magnum opus nothing but a chore

parts.note: a don is a university academic
a key work is a central or greatest piece of work

explanation.surface: A scholar's great book turns out to be mere drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, tedious drudgery, the routine labour nobody wants, is called this.

clue.text: Welsh ducks to boost market

indicators.note: ducks means dodges out, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to swell is to boost or increase

explanation.surface: Welsh ducks are promoted to lift trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh ducks' looks like poultry; it says the letter W ducks out of SWELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To market goods is to offer them to buyers, to sell them.

clue.text: Guardian backing others with utmost confidence

indicators.note: in a down clue, backing means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the Guardian newspaper, which sets this puzzle, calls itself us
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: A guardian supporting other people does so with total certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's newspaper refers to itself as US, so 'Guardian' gives US, reversed to SU.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the most certain is the superlative of being confident, as in 'surest way'.

clue.text: Pay for social bash where many get their kicks?

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay for it
a ball is a formal social dance
to club someone is to bash them

explanation.surface: Someone pays for a party at a place where many find excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social bash' reads as one party but is two pieces: a dance, then a verb for hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Footballers kick the ball, so a soccer team's organisation is where many get their kicks, a pun on thrills.

clue.text: Found fake depot

definitions.meaning: to found an argument on something is to rest it on that

explanation.surface: A discovered forged warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: ground something on, counterfeit (as base coin), and a camp or headquarters.

clue.text: Elevated cleric unknown to a large extent

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the word is raised up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a member of the clergy
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A promoted clergyman, unknown to many.
explanation.definitionFit: An intensifying adverb meaning extremely, greatly or highly.

clue.text: Innate ability to grasp reading or writing of ancient language

indicators.note: to grasp means to hold within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a nose for something is a natural talent for it
reading and writing are two of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A natural gift for understanding the reading or writing of an old tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' are reading, writing and arithmetic, so either of the first two gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of medieval Scandinavia and the Vikings, from which Icelandic descends.

clue.text: Additional area in shop for ceramics

indicators.note: in means the two pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: a store is a shop
new means additional, as in a new recruit

explanation.surface: An extension in a shop for pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense, hard-fired pottery is one of the main kinds of ceramics.

clue.text: Fears what hairstylist might produce

definitions.meaning: a verb: is afraid of, ... in the sense of fears
the rope-like hairstyle, short for dreadlocks

explanation.surface: A worry about what a hairdresser might do to your hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearing is dreading; and dreadlocks, shortened, are a style a hairdresser may create.

clue.text: Silly billy smuggling article without a thought

indicators.note: smuggling means the article is carried inside the other letters
silly means foolish or muddled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow carries contraband without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' scrambles the name to BLILY, and 'smuggling' slips the article inside it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting carelessly, unconcerned with consequences, is doing something with no worry or reflection.
